key_insight: Representation changes can preserve quantum correctness while silently removing high-level structure, which makes later synthesis choices unavailable.
engineering_relevance: For quantum compilers and workflows, preserving equivalence is not enough; tooling must also preserve or verify synthesis-relevant operations to avoid degraded circuits and lost optimization opportunities.
method: Compared Qiskit, TKET, and Cirq using controlled experiments, repository analysis, captured test circuits, and an MQT pipeline.
Tracked when high-level operations survive serialization, compiler conversion, and OpenQASM interchange.
Introduced Verified, which records operations before conversion and reconstructs them only after checking that the record still matches the delivered circuit.
evidence_signal: Across 360 OpenQASM delivery conditions, requested synthesis had no effect after direct OpenQASM 3 round trips, while Verified restored requested synthesis in all 830 recovery runs.
watch_item: The verification check can reject some valid records, so a practical implementation may trade completeness for safety.
paper_title: When Equivalent Quantum Circuits Lose Synthesis Choices
